The generalization to an arbitrary property Phi of the floor vector is true. Because each V_i is continuous and non-decreasing, the floor vector F(t) is right-locally constant. So if t* = inf of {t >= 0 : Phi(F(t))}, any t_n in the set decreasing to t* eventually has F(t_n) = F(t*), and Phi(F(t*)) holds. This is exactly the source argument ('the reasoning for the second set is the same'), so it is not a stronger claim.

I checked the encoding 'all floors >= 1 and eta <= ((1/n) sum 1/floor_i)^{-1}' against the source convention 1/0 = infinity. With W_i non-decreasing, the floors are all <= 0 for t < tbar_{k-1} and all >= 0 for t >= tbar_{k-1}. Then a zero floor gives harmonic mean 0 < eta, all-negative floors give a negative mean < eta, and all floors >= 1 is the ordinary case. So the encoded set equals the source set for every eta > 0 and monotone W. The instance used (W = V, eta >= 1) satisfies both.
